Samples
Product Samples from China: What to Check Before Production
Learn how to use samples to identify problems before placing a larger order.
Samples are not a formality. They are an opportunity to clarify specifications, compare suppliers, test the product, and record the standard that production should follow.
The sample conversation

Before a sample is made, clarify what is included in the sample price, whether the sample is handmade or production-representative, the material and dimensions, packaging, revisions, and delivery timing.
A useful sample review

Review function, appearance, dimensions, materials, color, labeling, packaging, and any feature that could affect safety or customer expectations. Keep photos and written notes so feedback is precise.
From approval to production
An approved sample should be connected to a written specification. Approval does not replace destination-market compliance, testing, or the need for production checks.

Factory checks
Factory and Supplier Checks in China
Understand what an on-the-ground check can and cannot tell you.
A factory visit can make supplier communication more concrete, especially when the project is large, complex, customized, or difficult to assess from photographs and messages alone.
When a visit can help

A visit may be appropriate when the order is significant, the product is customized, the process is technically important, or you need to clarify production capability and working arrangements before committing.
What a visit can examine

A visit can help document the facility, production flow, equipment, sample room, materials, packaging, communication, and questions raised by the buyer. The exact scope should be agreed before travel.
What it cannot guarantee
A visit is a snapshot, not a guarantee of every future production run. A buyer should still use specifications, samples, contracts, quality checks, and appropriate testing.

Quality control
Quality Control for Products Made in China
A plain-language guide to checking quality before goods leave the factory.

Quality control works best when expectations are defined before production. A check is only meaningful when it compares the goods with an approved sample, specification, drawing, or measurable requirement.
Define quality before production

Record the critical dimensions, materials, colors, functions, tolerances, labels, packaging, and acceptable defects. Separate critical requirements from preferences so the supplier understands priorities.
Different checkpoints

Depending on the project, checks may cover samples, materials, production progress, finished goods, packaging, and loading. The right timing depends on the product, schedule, and consequences of a late correction.
Reporting problems
A useful report identifies the requirement, the observed condition, evidence, affected quantity, and proposed corrective action. It should help the buyer and supplier decide what happens next.
